content:
Hello there


You can configure this setting in the following places. Follow the steps below in this order to address the issue:


1.Check the message filters.


2.Check the junk email settings:

Right-click your email account in the left-hand column and choose Settings.

Under the account name, click Junk.

On the right-hand side, under the heading "Destination and Retention," check where junk messages are being moved. Is this accidentally set to the Trash folder instead of the Junk folder?

If the folder is correct, but all email is still being treated as spam, temporarily uncheck the option "Enable adaptive junk mail controls for this account" to test if the behavior stops.


3.Check for synchronisation conflicts with other devices (POP and IMAP):

The POP issue: If another device connects via the POP protocol and is set to delete messages from the server after downloading, the server's inbox will be emptied.

The result in Thunderbird: Because Thunderbird works via IMAP, the program sees that the server inbox is empty and that the mail on the server has been moved to the trash.

Thunderbird synchronises this immediately and moves the mail to the local trash folder as well.

Solution: Check the mail settings on your devices and ensure they are either set to IMAP or that the option "Leave messages on the server" is enabled.


4.Check webmail for these errors. 5.Repair corrupted folder indexes .

content:
It sounds like you are not actually connecting to the server. So first you need to see if there is anything that could be blocking the access.

Q: Did you get a download of Thunderbird from the official website : https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/

or via 'Windows App Store' ?

This info would be useful to know as Windows App Store does not store the Thunderbird profile in the same place as Thunderbird if downloaded from website.

Firewall:

Do not disable Firewall as it may mean the default takes over and it's no use if it's disabled.

Firewall may be controlled by default installed with OS or it might be controlled by an Anti-Virus product you installed.

  • Exit Thunderbird
  • Access Firewall
  • The Thunderbird program must be set up as an 'Allowed' program.
  • Please confirm Thunderbird is set up as allowed program in the Firewall settings.


VPN Please check computer for a VPN. Many servers do not like a VPN because it hides your IP address and server may think you might be illegally trying to access account. Many Anti-Virus products now come with a VPN and in some cases it gets auto enabled. So please check and switch it off.

Anti-Virus: Q: What Anti-Virus are you using ?

If you have installed Avast or AVG - please disable the Mail Shield - it is notorious for causing problems with accessing emails.

I would also recommend you access the Anti-Virus and make an exemption to not scan anything in the 'Thunderbird' folder containing Profiles - this should also mean it would not scan anything within that folder. Imap accounts have files that are in a constant communication with server, opening files every time you download, send, select a folder or email etc etc and this can cause interruption to processes.

Server Settings: It looks like you are using the correct server settings for an imap account.
